subject: Mathematics
content: To factorise a quadratic trinomial x² + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b. Write the trinomial as (x + m)(x + n) where m·n = c and m + n = b. Always check the factorisation by expanding the brackets. Example: x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3) because 2 × 3 = 6 and 2 + 3 = 5.

subject: Mathematics
content: Always take out the highest common factor first before any other factorisation. For four-term expressions, group terms in pairs and take a common factor from each pair, then factor out the common bracket. Example: ax + ay + bx + by = a(x + y) + b(x + y) = (a + b)(x + y).

subject: Mathematics
content: A difference of two squares factorises as a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This only works for a difference, never a sum, of squares. Look for it after removing common factors. Example: 9x² − 25 = (3x − 5)(3x + 5).

subject: Mathematics
content: When a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 cannot be factorised easily, use the quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a). First write the equation in standard form, identify a, b and c with their signs, then substitute. The discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac tells you the nature of the roots: Δ > 0 gives two real roots, Δ = 0 one repeated real root, Δ < 0 no real roots.

subject: Mathematics
content: To complete the square for x² + bx, add and subtract (b/2)²: x² + bx = (x + b/2)² − (b/2)². Used to solve quadratics, find turning points of parabolas, and derive the quadratic formula. If the coefficient of x² is not 1, first divide the whole equation by it.

subject: Mathematics
content: Laws of exponents: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1; a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ. For equations with the unknown in the exponent, write both sides with the same base and equate exponents. Rational exponents link to surds: a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(aᵐ).

subject: Mathematics
content: Arithmetic sequence: constant difference d, general term Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, sum Sₙ = n/2 (2a + (n − 1)d). Geometric sequence: constant ratio r, general term Tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹, sum Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1). An infinite geometric series converges only when −1 < r < 1, with sum S∞ = a/(1 − r).

subject: Mathematics
content: The derivative from first principles is f′(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x + h) − f(x)] / h. Substitute f(x + h), expand, simplify until h can be cancelled from the fraction, then let h → 0. For f(x) = x², f′(x) = lim(h→0)(2xh + h²)/h = lim(h→0)(2x + h) = 2x.

subject: Mathematics
content: Power rule: if f(x) = axⁿ then f′(x) = naxⁿ⁻¹. Differentiate term by term. The derivative gives the gradient of the tangent, so stationary points occur where f′(x) = 0. Use the sign of f′ or the shape of the cubic to classify maxima and minima in curve sketching and optimisation problems.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Financial mathematics: compound interest and depreciation
content: Compound growth: A = P(1 + i)ⁿ where i is the interest rate per period and n the number of periods. Depreciation on a reducing balance: A = P(1 − i)ⁿ. For interest compounded monthly, divide the annual rate by 12 and multiply the years by 12. Solve for n using logarithms: n = log(A/P) / log(1 + i).

subject: Mathematics
content: The parabola y = a(x − p)² + q has turning point (p; q) and axis of symmetry x = p. If a > 0 it opens upwards (minimum q); if a < 0 it opens downwards (maximum q). From standard form y = ax² + bx + c, the axis of symmetry is x = −b/(2a) and the y-intercept is c. x-intercepts are found by setting y = 0.

subject: Mathematics
content: The hyperbola y = a/(x − p) + q has asymptotes x = p and y = q. The exponential function y = a·bˣ⁻ᵖ + q (b > 0, b ≠ 1) has horizontal asymptote y = q; it grows when b > 1 and decays when 0 < b < 1. Sketch by finding asymptotes, intercepts and one extra point.

subject: Mathematics
content: Fundamental identities: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. To prove an identity, work with the more complicated side, write everything in terms of sin and cos, and simplify using these identities. State restrictions where denominators would be zero, e.g. cos θ ≠ 0 for tan θ.

subject: Mathematics
content: In a right-angled triangle: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent (SOH-CAH-TOA). Use these to find unknown sides and angles. The hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle and is the longest side.

subject: Mathematics
content: For any events, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B). Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together, so P(A and B) = 0. Independent events satisfy P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). The complementary rule: P(not A) = 1 − P(A). The fundamental counting principle: if one choice can be made in m ways and a second in n ways, together they can be made in m × n ways.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Statistics: measures of central tendency and spread
content: The mean is the sum of values divided by the count; the median is the middle value of ordered data; the mode is the most frequent value. The five-number summary (minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum) draws a box-and-whisker plot. The interquartile range IQR = Q3 − Q1 measures spread and is resistant to outliers.

subject: Accounting
content: The accounting equation is Assets = Owner's Equity + Liabilities (A = OE + L). Every transaction affects the equation but keeps it balanced. Analyse each transaction by asking which accounts are affected, whether each is an asset, equity or liability, and whether it increases or decreases. Income increases equity; expenses and drawings decrease equity.

subject: Accounting
content: Key ratios: gross profit percentage on sales = gross profit / sales × 100; current ratio = current assets : current liabilities; acid-test ratio excludes inventory from current assets. The current ratio tests short-term liquidity — around 2:1 is generally healthy, while below 1:1 signals the business may struggle to pay short-term debts.
